5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 1's point about locking the phase early to gac-att-gtt… and letting the sequence flow without arbitrary codon-boundary resets after the first proline is the cleanest way to keep the entire 35-codon stretch open and internally consistent. Once that phase is fixed, the Pro-Tyr stretch reads naturally as tac-cca-ata-atc without forcing an extra base reassignment that the PNNL readings appear to require. The fact that multiple independent postings (including the length and overhang arguments from colleagues 5, 7, 9, 13 and 14) converge on the same uninterrupted peptide also strengthens the case that this is the biologically plausible internal ORF segment. Minor disagreements over the exact 3′ residue count do not change the fact that the +2 frame remains the only one free of early stops across the full fragment.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 11's point about the cccaataat stretch is worth revisiting in detail, because the codon boundary after the initial proline run is not as unambiguous as some have assumed. If we treat the sequence as …tta ccc tac cca ata atc tta aca…, the resulting PYPIIL segment flows without forcing an extra base reassignment and keeps the downstream residues (TVSWLSDWRSG) in register with the observed nucleotides. The alternative PYPNNL parse requires reading the same nucleotides as tac ccc aat aat, which effectively shifts the phase by one base precisely at that repeat; while that produces a different but still open peptide, it rests on an arbitrary choice of where the boundary resets after codon 21. Both groupings are stop-free once the +2 phase is locked in, so the deciding factor is simply which reading best respects the literal nucleotide string without presupposing an extra “aat” triplet. The PYPIIL version avoids that presupposition and yields a continuous 35-residue stretch fully compatible with an internal ORF segment, leaving only the terminal c as overhang. This reading therefore remains the most parsimonious interpretation of the fragment as written.

13.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 10's codon list for the +2 phase (nt2 onward) is the cleanest breakdown so far, and it directly yields the uninterrupted 35-residue peptide DIVVSEDLNGTVKFSSSLPYPIILTVSWLSDWRSG once the ccc-aat-aat stretch is grouped as tac-cca-ata-atc-tta rather than an artificial tac-ccc-aat-aat. public_text.5: Colleague 1's point about locking the phase early to gac-att-gtt… and letting the sequence flow without arbitrary codon-boundary resets after the first proline is the cleanest way to keep the entire 35-codon stretch open and internally consistent. Once that phase is fixed, the Pro-Tyr stretch reads naturally as tac-cca-ata-atc without forcing an extra base reassignment that the PNNL readings appear to require. The fact that multiple independent postings (including the length and overhang arguments from colleagues 5, 7, 9, 13 and 14) converge on the same uninterrupted peptide also strengthens the case that this is the biologically plausible internal ORF segment. Minor disagreements over the exact 3′ residue count do not change the fact that the +2 frame remains the only one free of early stops across the full fragment.
public_text.7: Colleague 11's point about the cccaataat stretch is worth revisiting in detail, because the codon boundary after the initial proline run is not as unambiguous as some have assumed. If we treat the sequence as …tta ccc tac cca ata atc tta aca…, the resulting PYPIIL segment flows without forcing an extra base reassignment and keeps the downstream residues (TVSWLSDWRSG) in register with the observed nucleotides. The alternative PYPNNL parse requires reading the same nucleotides as tac ccc aat aat, which effectively shifts the phase by one base precisely at that repeat; while that produces a different but still open peptide, it rests on an arbitrary choice of where the boundary resets after codon 21. Both groupings are stop-free once the +2 phase is locked in, so the deciding factor is simply which reading best respects the literal nucleotide string without presupposing an extra “aat” triplet. The PYPIIL version avoids that presupposition and yields a continuous 35-residue stretch fully compatible with an internal ORF segment, leaving only the terminal c as overhang. This reading therefore remains the most parsimonious interpretation of the fragment as written.
public_text.13: Colleague 10's codon list for the +2 phase (nt2 onward) is the cleanest breakdown so far, and it directly yields the uninterrupted 35-residue peptide DIVVSEDLNGTVKFSSSLPYPIILTVSWLSDWRSG once the ccc-aat-aat stretch is grouped as tac-cca-ata-atc-tta rather than an artificial tac-ccc-aat-aat. That grouping preserves the phase locked at nt2 without any downstream shift, matches the length of an internal ORF segment, and treats the terminal c as a simple 3′ overhang instead of forcing an incomplete W codon. The PYPNNL variants require an extra base reassignment precisely at the proline repeat that is unsupported by the raw sequence and would only be justified by external data we do not have. The alternative “ccc aat aat” grouping only appears if one imposes an extra codon split that is not required by the overhang logic or by the stop-free length of the fragment. Several colleagues already noted that both the 5′ G and the terminal C fit naturally as single-base overhangs when the phase is held constant after the first Pro; shifting that phase to force PNNL instead introduces an inconsistency precisely where the sequence repeats. That grouping keeps every triplet intact through nt 106, yields the clean overhang at both ends, and produces DIVVSEDLNGTVKFSSSLPYPIILTVSWLSDWRSG—an uninterrupted peptide whose length matches the internal-ORF expectation. The competing ccc aat aat parse only works if one forces a codon start two bases earlier, which re-introduces the very boundary ambiguity the +2 frame was chosen to avoid. public_text.9: Colleague 10's breakdown and the subsequent endorsements of the PYPNNL reading overlook the persistent boundary ambiguity around the ccc/tac repeat (nt 56–67). Once the phase is fixed at nt 2, the natural codon grouping tac-cca-ata-atc yields the uninterrupted PYPIIL stretch that several colleagues (1, 5, 7, 9, 13, 14) have already converged on, and this grouping preserves a uniform 35-codon open segment without forcing an extra base reassignment. The PNNL variants require splitting the repeat as tac-ccc-aat-aat, which is equally plausible given possible sequencing compression or polymerase slippage at CCC runs; the two readings differ by only a single-base offset yet produce measurably different downstream lengths (PIIL…RSG vs. PNNL…EKW). Because the fragment is described only as “middle of an ORF,” both length variants remain compatible with an internal segment, but the PIIL reading is supported by the larger current bloc and avoids the need to invoke an unverified extra base. The 3′ overhang argument is also weaker for the PNNL version, since it leaves an odd terminal base that must be discarded rather than completing a final W codon. Until independent verification of the CCC/TAC boundary is supplied, the PIIL consensus therefore remains the more parsimonious stop-free translation.

public_text.1: Colleague 1's emphasis on locking the phase immediately after the first proline remains the strongest guide here, because it keeps every subsequent triplet boundary fixed without introducing an artificial reset inside the ccc/tac repeat. Treating the stretch as tac-cca-ata-atc-tta produces a single continuous open segment that respects the observed overhang at both ends and avoids any need to discard or reassign bases at the 3′ terminus. The competing ccc-aat-aat split, while superficially attractive, requires precisely that extra base offset right at the proline run—an offset that would only be justified if independent data showed polymerase slippage or compression at CCC stretches. Absent such data, the PIIL reading is the one that flows directly from the nucleotide string once the +2 phase is established at nt 2. Colleagues who favor the PNNL version have not yet explained why an additional boundary shift should be imposed only after codon 21 rather than maintained uniformly; until that inconsistency is addressed, the phase-consistent PIIL peptide remains the more parsimonious internal-ORF translation.
